title: Ontong Java Plateau eruption
summary: The Ontong Java Plateau in the southwestern Pacific is described as the largest of the world's large igneous provinces, with an area of about 1.6 million square kilometres. Ocean Drilling Program basement lavas record eruptive episodes at 122 ± 3 and 90 ± 4 million years, while newer argon dating of dredged rocks gives ages of about 96 to 116 million years.

uncertainty.note: Start and end are the two eruptive episodes in the ODP Leg 192 prospectus (122 ± 3 Ma and 90 ± 4 Ma). Tejada et al. (2023) report 40Ar-39Ar ages of ~96-116 Ma, with one dredge sample at 115.56 ± 0.36 Ma; the id uses 120 Ma. Years are Ma counted back from the present with no 1950 offset.

as_recorded.value: ~96–116 Ma and 67–68 Ma 40Ar-39Ar age data; 115.56 ± 0.36 Ma for sample D3-02

when.display: c. 122–90 million years ago (two eruptive episodes)

where.modern_name: Ontong Java Plateau, southwestern Pacific Ocean, north of the Solomon Islands
where.historical_name: Ontong Java Plateau on the Pacific plate, Cretaceous; no polities exist at this date

importance.justification: Described as the largest of the world's large igneous provinces, a single huge volcanic outpouring on the Pacific seafloor.
